notes.heading: Combustion of metals and non-metals
points: Fuel + oxygen gives oxide plus heat. Reactive metals: 4Li + O2 → 2Li2O; 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO (bright white light).
The metal is oxidized (Li → Li+ + e; Mg → Mg2+ + 2e) and oxygen is reduced (O2 + 4e → 2O2−).
Non-metals form non-metal oxides: non-metal + oxygen → non-metal oxide. Sulfur burns to SO2: S + O2 → SO2.
Sulfur impurities in fossil fuels give SO2, then SO3 (2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3), then H2SO4 with water: SO3 + H2O → H2SO4.

notes.heading: Complete combustion of hydrocarbons and alcohols
points: Excess oxygen: organic compound + O2 → CO2 + H2O; the reaction is exothermic.
Alkanes: CnH2n+2 + (3n+1)/2 O2 → nCO2 + (n+1)H2O. Alcohols: CnH2n+1OH + 3n/2 O2 → nCO2 + (n+1)H2O.
Water may be liquid or steam depending on temperature, so state symbols vary with conditions.
Examples: octane ΔcH = −5470 kJ mol−1; ethanol C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O, ΔcH = −1367 kJ mol−1.

notes.heading: Incomplete combustion products
points: Occurs when oxygen is limiting, e.g. in car engines. Products are CO and/or C (soot) plus water.
Alkane to CO: CnH2n+2 + (2n+1)/2 O2 → nCO + (n+1)H2O. Alkane to C: CnH2n+2 + (n+1)/2 O2 → nC + (n+1)H2O.
Methane: CH4 + 3/2 O2 → CO + 2H2O; CH4 + O2 → C + 2H2O.
CO is poisonous: it binds irreversibly to hemoglobin, cutting the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity. Soot shows as black deposit on glassware.
Incomplete combustion releases less heat than complete combustion of the same fuel.

notes.heading: Fossil fuels: pros, cons, specific energy
points: Fossil fuels are coal, crude oil and natural gas; they are non-renewable and used for electricity and engines.
Burning them releases CO2, a greenhouse gas that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation, raising global temperature.
Specific energy is heat released per unit mass of fuel (MJ kg−1); wood is lowest of common fuels.
Longer hydrocarbon chains are more prone to incomplete combustion (lower volatility, stronger London forces), giving CO/soot and less energy per mass.
Fossil fuels also release SOx from sulfur impurities, a further environmental problem.

notes.heading: Biofuels and photosynthesis
points: Biofuels come from organic compounds made from CO2 by biological carbon fixation, such as photosynthesis, over a short time.
Photosynthesis: 6CO2 + 6H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2, with light absorbed by chlorophyll.
Fermentation: C6H12O6 → 2C2H5OH + 2CO2. CO2 released is offset by CO2 absorbed during growth.
Advantages: renewable, lower net greenhouse emissions, less dependence on imported oil, wide range of plant materials usable.
Disadvantages: farmland, water and fertilizer use; less food production; monocultures cut biodiversity; possible deforestation; high cost; lower energy per mass or volume.

notes.heading: Fuel cells: hydrogen and methanol
points: A fuel cell converts a fuel's chemical energy directly to electrical energy; fuel is supplied continuously from outside, unlike a voltaic cell.
Hydrogen cell anode: H2 → 2H+ + 2e. Cathode: O2 + 4e + 4H+ → 2H2O. Overall: 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O.
Electrons travel through the external circuit; H+ ions pass across the membrane. The only product is water.
Hydrogen must be made, by electrolysis of water or steam reforming of hydrocarbons, which gives CO and CO2.
Methanol cell anode: CH3OH + H2O → CO2 + 6H+ + 6e. Cathode: 3/2 O2 + 6H+ + 6e → 3H2O. Overall: CH3OH + 3/2 O2 → CO2 + 2H2O.
Methanol: higher energy density, liquid and easier to store. Drawbacks: produces CO2, toxic, expensive precious-metal catalyst.

definitions.definition: A reaction in which a fuel reacts with oxygen, releasing heat energy; the fuel is oxidized to oxides.
definitions.trap: Calling combustion endothermic; it is always exothermic.

definitions.definition: Burning of a fuel when oxygen is limited, producing carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) instead of only carbon dioxide, plus water.
definitions.trap: Forgetting that water is still produced and that it releases less energy.

definitions.definition: The amount of heat energy released per unit mass of a fuel, in MJ kg−1.
definitions.trap: Mixing it up with energy density, which is per unit volume.

definitions.definition: The amount of energy released per unit volume of a fuel, in MJ dm−3.
definitions.trap: Mixing it up with specific energy, which is per mass.

definitions.definition: A renewable fuel produced from organic compounds formed by biological carbon fixation, such as ethanol made from plants.
definitions.trap: Saying biofuels release no CO2 on burning; the CO2 is offset by earlier absorption.

definitions.definition: The production of organic compounds from carbon dioxide in living organisms, for example photosynthesis.
definitions.trap: Confusing it with fermentation, which releases CO2.

definitions.definition: An electrochemical cell that converts the chemical energy of a fuel directly into electrical energy, with fuel continuously supplied from outside.
definitions.trap: Saying it stores reactants inside like a voltaic cell.

definitions.definition: Greenhouse gases absorb infrared radiation and re-emit it, some towards Earth's surface, which traps heat and raises global temperature.
definitions.trap: Claiming N2 and O2 absorb infrared; they do not.

definitions.definition: The tendency of a substance to change state from liquid to gas.
definitions.trap: Thinking longer alkane chains are more volatile; they are less volatile.
